This is an openEO UDF (User Defined Function).
https://open-eo.github.io/openeo-python-client/udf.html

It targets the "python" runtime, version 3.11.
https://openeofed.dataspace.copernicus.eu/?discover=0&udf-runtime=Python
"""

from typing import TypedDict

import numpy as np
import xarray as xr

from openeo.udf import inspect

LOG_CODE = "binary_operator"


class Context(TypedDict):
    operator: str
    argument: float | int


OPERATORS = {
    "gte": np.greater_equal,
    "gt": np.greater,
    "lte": np.less_equal,
    "lt": np.less,
}


def apply_datacube(cube: xr.DataArray, context: Context) -> xr.DataArray:
    """
    Apply a binary (2 argument) operator to a cube.

    Example:

    ```
    context.operator = "gte"
    context.argument = 30
    result = (cube >= 30)
    ```

    Why not just use native openEO processes?
    Because there seems to be a bug related to Parameters.
    https://forum.dataspace.copernicus.eu/t/udp-parameter-not-applied/5282/3

    Arguments:
        cube: xarray DataArray
        context: user-provided arguments.
    """
    # parse and validate context
    operator_name = context["operator"]
    try:
        operator = OPERATORS[operator_name]
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid operator: {operator_name}")

    argument = context["argument"]
    if not isinstance(argument, float | int):
        raise TypeError(f"Invalid argument: {argument}")

    inspect(
        message=f"applying {operator_name}(cube, {argument})",
        code=LOG_CODE,
        level="debug",
    )

    return operator(cube, argument)

"""
This is an openEO UDF (User Defined Function).
https://open-eo.github.io/openeo-python-client/udf.html

It targets the "python" runtime, version 3.11.
https://openeofed.dataspace.copernicus.eu/?discover=0&udf-runtime=Python
"""

import warnings
from typing import TypedDict

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr
from openeo.metadata import Band, CollectionMetadata

from openeo.udf import inspect

LOG_CODE = "monthly_climatology"


class Context(TypedDict):
    target_band: str

    # baseline period over which to compute the climatology
    # inclusive
    # iso8601 date string
    baseline_start: str
    baseline_end: str

    # replace small standard deviations with this value
    # e.g. where there is only a single observation in the baseline period
    std_min: float


BAND_DIM = "bands"
CALENDAR_MONTHS = np.arange(1, 13)


def _as_datetime_index(t_index: pd.Index) -> pd.DatetimeIndex:
    if isinstance(t_index, pd.DatetimeIndex):
        return t_index
    return pd.to_datetime(t_index)


def _calendar_months(t_coord: xr.DataArray) -> xr.DataArray:
    """Calendar month (1-12) for each time label.

    Returns:
        DataArray with dims [t], aligned to `t_coord`.
    """
    months = _as_datetime_index(t_coord.indexes["t"]).month
    return xr.DataArray(months, coords={"t": t_coord}, dims="t")


def _monthly_climatology(
    baseline: xr.DataArray, std_min: float
) -> tuple[xr.DataArray, xr.DataArray]:
    """Per calendar month: median and population std over baseline timesteps.

    Arguments:
        baseline: Single-band cube, typically [x, y, t].
        std_min: Lower bound applied to std where baseline samples exist.

    Returns:
        (clim_median, clim_std): two DataArrays with the same dimensionality.
        We drop the `t` dimension, and add a `month` dimension with 12 months.
        Months with no baseline timestep (or only NaN values) are NaN.
    """
    month = _calendar_months(baseline.coords["t"]).rename("month")
    by_month = baseline.assign_coords(month=month).groupby("month")

    clim_median = by_month.median(dim="t", skipna=True)

    # For an all-NaN month, numpy logs:
    # RuntimeWarning: Degrees of freedom <= 0 for slice.
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.filterwarnings(
            "ignore",
            message="Degrees of freedom <= 0 for slice.",
            category=RuntimeWarning,
        )
        clim_std = by_month.std(dim="t", skipna=True, ddof=0)

    # ensure we have all 12 months
    clim_median = clim_median.reindex(month=CALENDAR_MONTHS)
    clim_std = clim_std.reindex(month=CALENDAR_MONTHS)

    clim_std = clim_std.clip(min=std_min)

    return clim_median, clim_std


def _broadcast_to_timesteps(
    clim: xr.DataArray, t_coord: xr.DataArray
) -> xr.DataArray:
    """Map per-month climatology onto every time step.

    Arguments:
        clim: Climatology field with dims [x, y, month]
        t_coord: Time coordinate for the output series (typically all timesteps in the cube).

    Returns:
        DataArray with dims [x, y, t]. Each label along `t` gets the clim value for
        its calendar month (January timesteps all share the month=1 climatology).
    """
    month_of_t = _calendar_months(t_coord)
    return clim.sel(month=month_of_t)


def apply_datacube(cube: xr.DataArray, context: Context) -> xr.DataArray:
    """
    Compute a monthly median and standard deviation climatology.

    Assuming `cube` has dimensions [x, y, t, bands].
    Filter to target_band.

    This monthly climatology would normally have some "temporal" dimension
    of length 12 (Jan, Feb, ..., Dec).
    But here we retain the time (t) dimension as-is, broadcasting
    the climatology values back to match each individual time step.

    Arguments:
        cube: xarray DataArray
        context: user-provided arguments.

    Returns:
        xarray DataArray with dimensions [x, y, t, bands].
        bands = [target_band, target_band_median, target_band_std]
    """
    target_band = context["target_band"]
    baseline_start = context["baseline_start"]
    baseline_end = context["baseline_end"]
    std_min = context["std_min"]
    inspect(
        message=f"applying {LOG_CODE} to {target_band} with baseline={baseline_start} to {baseline_end} and std_min={std_min}",
        code=LOG_CODE,
        level="debug",
    )

    if BAND_DIM not in cube.dims:
        raise ValueError(f"Expected band dimension {BAND_DIM!r}, got dims {cube.dims!r}")
    if target_band not in cube.coords[BAND_DIM].values:
        raise ValueError(f"Band {target_band!r} not in {list(cube.coords[BAND_DIM].values)!r}")

    values = cube.sel({BAND_DIM: target_band}, drop=True)
    t = cube.coords["t"]
    t_index = cube.indexes["t"]
    if isinstance(t_index, pd.DatetimeIndex):
        t_dt = t_index
    else:
        inspect(
            message=(
                f"{LOG_CODE}: t index is {type(t_index).__name__} "
                f"(dtype={getattr(t_index, 'dtype', None)!r}), not DatetimeIndex; "
                "parsing with pd.to_datetime"
            ),
            code=LOG_CODE,
            level="warning",
        )
        t_dt = pd.to_datetime(t_index)
    baseline_start_ts = pd.Timestamp(baseline_start)
    baseline_end_ts = pd.Timestamp(baseline_end)
    in_baseline = (t_dt >= baseline_start_ts) & (t_dt <= baseline_end_ts)
    baseline = values.sel(t=t[in_baseline])

    clim_median, clim_std = _monthly_climatology(baseline, std_min)
    median_t = _broadcast_to_timesteps(clim_median, t)
    std_t = _broadcast_to_timesteps(clim_std, t)

    median_band = f"{target_band}_median"
    std_band = f"{target_band}_std"
    median_t = median_t.assign_coords(bands=median_band).expand_dims(BAND_DIM)
    std_t = std_t.assign_coords(bands=std_band).expand_dims(BAND_DIM)
    values_out = values.assign_coords(bands=target_band).expand_dims(BAND_DIM)

    out = xr.concat(
        [values_out, median_t, std_t],
        dim=BAND_DIM,
    )
    return out.transpose(*cube.dims)


def apply_metadata(
    metadata: CollectionMetadata, context: Context
) -> CollectionMetadata:
    """
    Returns the expected cube metadata, after applying this UDF, based on input metadata.
    """
    target_band = context["target_band"]
    metadata = metadata.filter_bands([target_band])
    metadata = metadata.append_band(
        Band(
            name=f"{target_band}_median",
        )
    )
    metadata = metadata.append_band(
        Band(
            name=f"{target_band}_std",
        )
    )
    return metadata

"""

https://open-eo.github.io/openeo-python-client/udf.html

It targets the "python" runtime, version 3.11.
https://openeofed.dataspace.copernicus.eu/?discover=0&udf-runtime=Python
"""

from typing import TypedDict

import numpy as np
import scipy
import xarray as xr

from openeo.udf import inspect

LOG_CODE = "connectivity_filter"


class Context(TypedDict):
    min_pixels: int


def format_bytes(bytes_val: float) -> str:
    for unit in ["B", "KB", "MB", "GB", "TB"]:
        if bytes_val < 1024:
            return f"{bytes_val:.2f} {unit}"
        bytes_val /= 1024
    return f"{bytes_val:.2f} PB"


def small_region_mask(input_array: np.ndarray, min_pixels: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Use scipy.ndimage.label to detect features (clusters of non-zero valued pixels).

    Arguments:
        input_array: a 2D (spatial) boolean array / mask.
            1 = valid pixel. 0 = ignored pixel.
        min_pixels: once clustered into features, exclude features smaller than min_pixels

    Returns:
        a boolean mask of pixels to exclude, based on a minimum feature size.
        1 = excluded pixel.
    """
    if input_array.dtype != bool:
        raise TypeError("input_array must have dtype bool")
    if min_pixels < 1:
        raise ValueError("min_pixels must be 1 or greater")

    # 8-connectivity (diagonals count)
    structure = np.ones((3, 3))

    # https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.ndimage.label.html#scipy.ndimage.label
    # labelled_features has same shape as input_array.
    # with clusters of pixels labelled by feature id (integer).
    # feature id 0 = pixels not belonging to a feature, because their value in input_array is 0.
    # the first cluster of pixels has feature id = 1.
    labelled_features, _ = scipy.ndimage.label(input_array, structure=structure)

    # 1D array.
    # label_counts[i] is number of pixels with feature id = i.
    label_counts = np.bincount(labelled_features.ravel())

    # map each feature id to a bool (whether it should be masked).
    # label_masked[i] is whether to mask feature id = i.
    labels_masked = label_counts < min_pixels

    # do not mask feature id = 0
    labels_masked[0] = False

    # numpy Integer array indexing https://numpy.org/doc/stable/user/basics.indexing.html#integer-array-indexing
    # for each pixel in labelled_features (pixel value = feature id)
    # do a positional lookup from labels_masked,
    # essentially mapping from feature id to the corresponding true/false from labels_masked.
    # mask has same shape as labelled_features, which has same shape as input_array
    mask = labels_masked[labelled_features]

    return mask


def filter_small_regions_2d(data: np.ndarray, min_pixels: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Mask out pixels belonging to 8-connected components smaller than min_pixels."""
    exclude = small_region_mask(data, min_pixels)
    return np.where(exclude, False, data)


def apply_datacube(cube: xr.DataArray, context: Context) -> xr.DataArray:
    """
    Remove pixels in spatially disconnected components smaller than min_pixels.

    Arguments:
        cube: xarray DataArray with spatial dimensions "x" and "y".
            Typically a boolean hotspot mask; non-bool values are treated as valid when non-zero.
        context: user-provided arguments (min_pixels).
    """
    inspect(
        data=cube.sizes, message="Input cube dimensions", code=LOG_CODE, level="debug"
    )
    inspect(
        message=f"Size of cube = {format_bytes(cube.nbytes)}",
        code=LOG_CODE,
        level="debug",
    )

    if cube.dtype != bool:
        inspect(
            message=f"expected dtype bool, got dtype {cube.dtype}", code=LOG_CODE, level="warning"
        )
        # try to convert from float
        cube = cube.notnull() & (cube != 0)

    if "x" not in cube.dims or "y" not in cube.dims:
        raise ValueError(f'Expected spatial dims "x" and "y", got {cube.dims!r}')

    min_pixels = context["min_pixels"]
    if not isinstance(min_pixels, int):
        raise TypeError("min_pixels should be an int")
    if min_pixels < 1:
        raise ValueError("min_pixels should be 1 or greater")

    total_pixels = cube.sizes["y"] * cube.sizes["x"]
    if min_pixels >= total_pixels:
        raise ValueError(
            "min_pixels should be less than or equal to the total number of pixels"
        )

    inspect(
        message=f"Applying connectivity filter with min_pixels = {min_pixels}",
        code=LOG_CODE,
        level="debug",
    )

    filtered: xr.DataArray = xr.apply_ufunc(
        filter_small_regions_2d,
        cube,
        input_core_dims=[["y", "x"]],
        output_core_dims=[["y", "x"]],
        vectorize=True,
        kwargs={"min_pixels": min_pixels},
    )

    inspect(
        message=f"returned dtype = {filtered.dtype}",
        code=LOG_CODE,
        level="debug",
    )

    return filtered.transpose(*cube.dims)

summary: Detect NDTI turbidity hotspots from Sentinel-2, then aggregate yearly hotspot and water-coverage statistics for upstream control zone and downstream influence zone.
description: Computes monthly median Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI) from Sentinel-2 L2A. Persistent water is masked with Joint Research Centre (JRC) Global Surface Water (GSW). A baseline climatology (median and std) drives per-month exceedance tests. Pixels with enough exceedance months per year become hotspots. Small 8-connected components are removed. Returns a vector cube with bands: sum(hotspot), count(hotspot), avg(hotspot), sum(hotspot_exceedance_count), count(hotspot_exceedance_count), avg(hotspot_exceedance_count), sum(water_valid), count(water_valid), avg(water_valid). WARNING: depending on the requested download format, bands may be named differently - see: https://forum.dataspace.copernicus.eu/t/inconsistent-band-names-csv-parquet/5683.

parameters.name: upstream_and_downstream
parameters.description: GeoJSON FeatureCollection containing the upstream control zone and downstream influence zone. Features should be polygons with a corresponding 'name' property.

parameters.name: temporal_extent
parameters.description: Temporal extent specified as two-element array with start and end date/date-time.

parameters.name: baseline_start
parameters.description: Start of the baseline period for climatology

parameters.name: baseline_end
parameters.description: End of the baseline period for climatology (inclusive).

parameters.name: water_occurrence_threshold
parameters.description: Minimum Joint Research Centre (JRC) Global Surface Water (GSW) occurrence (percent) for a pixel to be treated as water.

parameters.name: anomaly_z_threshold
parameters.description: For a pixel-month to count as anomalous, its NDTI Z-score must be greater than or equal to this value.

parameters.name: effect_threshold
parameters.description: For a pixel-month to count as anomalous, NDTI must be at least (1 + effect_threshold) times the climatological monthly median.

parameters.name: min_months_per_year_for_hotspot
parameters.description: Minimum number of anomalous months in a calendar year for a pixel to be flagged as a hotspot that year.

parameters.name: min_contiguous_pixels
parameters.description: Minimum 8-connected component size (pixels) for hotspot pixels. Isolated pixels are excluded.
